basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 2.' and it opens 'Vers. 2. Terror vester et tremor. Non homini praeposuit Deus hominem sed animantibus.'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 2. Terror vester et tremor. Non homini praeposuit Deus hominem sed animantibus. Neque enim dixit: Terror vester sit super homines, sed super animantia terrae: atque ideo, ut B. Gregorius dicit, supra modum superbire est ab aequali velle timeri. Omnes homines natura genuit aequales, sed meritorum distantia justo Dei judicio, sed occulto, alios aliis subjecit. Omnes pisces manui vestrae traditi sunt. Id est, potestati: Et omne quod movetur erit vobis in cibum. Post diluvium esus permissus est carnium. Antea enim pomis et oleribus vescebantur. Sed quia in diluvio terra virtutem suae fertilitatis amiserat, | ideo Deus consulens humanae fragilitati permisit homini vesci carnibus.
